- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially >0.44) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (sentiment <0.27) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lagged mean reversion: model often overreacts to recent highs/lows, then slowly drifts toward historical mean — adjust for 3–5 day lag in correction.
- Avoid overconfidence in short-term momentum — if sentiment is volatile, forecast should be more conservative and less steeply trending.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days, model should not assume sustained breakout — cap upward bias at +10–15% above recent high.
- If sentiment is negative and price is rising, model should not ignore sentiment — reduce forecast slope to avoid “sentiment-blind” overcorrection.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict late-period price — apply downward bias in final 5–7 days if sentiment is weak or neutral.
